data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues separation is unnecessary when verification is grounded in an external executor, but its stated 'Symbolic Anchor' mechanism does not establish independent verification of the CLAIM as the problem frames it; it only guarantees execution of the TEST. The same engine authors both the claim and the test, and SRC_002's own countercondition concedes circular testing as a live failure mode. Yet the claim still treats a third-party-determined pass/fail result as 'independent of the engine's training history.' The causal link is missing: an external interpreter deterministically executing a test the SAME engine wrote does not mechanistically show that the claim was checked by a different reasoning/training history; it only shows the test is self-consistent with the engine's own encoding. The problem asks whether separating authoring from checking engines is necessary for independent verification; SRC_002 substitutes 'separation of execution from authoring' for 'separation of checking engine from authoring engine' without arguing why the former entails the latter, and its countercondition shows exactly why it does not.
